gobeklitepe.name: Göbeklitepe
gobeklitepe.slogan: T-shaped giants, raised before anyone had invented the village.
gobeklitepe.line: Built around 9500 BCE, it is older than pottery, writing and the wheel; excavations began in 1995 and UNESCO listed it in 2018.

balikligol.name: Balıklıgöl
balikligol.slogan: A pool where Abraham's fire turned to water and the logs to carp.
balikligol.line: By legend, Nimrod threw Abraham into a fire here and God turned the flames into water and the logs into sacred carp.

harrankulturevi.name: Harran Beehive Houses
harrankulturevi.slogan: Mud-brick domes that keep the desert out, as they did for Abraham's neighbours.
harrankulturevi.line: A 2002 count found 2,760 beehive houses in Harran; their walls are 50 to 60 cm thick and each dome has a roof hole for ventilation.

urfakalesi.name: Urfa Castle
urfakalesi.slogan: Two Roman columns watching over the old town of Edessa.
urfakalesi.line: The citadel was renovated in 1462-3 under Uzun Hasan and again in 1638 on the orders of Ottoman sultan Murad IV.

sanliurfamuseum.name: Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum
sanliurfamuseum.slogan: Meet the man who stood in Urfa nearly eleven thousand years ago.
sanliurfamuseum.line: The Urfa Man, about 1.90 m tall and dated to around 9000 BC, is called the oldest naturalistic life-sized human sculpture.
